requirements.summary: The detector trips at the designed supply levels, with the designed hysteresis and delay, and does not chatter on a slow, rippled ramp.
A dip either produces one reset pulse of at least the analytic minimum width or produces nothing; the boundary follows the divider's RC constant.
Reset is released only after the supply reached the rising threshold, on a clock edge, after the configured number of clocks.
Whenever the detector falls, in any state and for any pulse width, every register is back at its reset value at once.
After release the controller waits, loads the straps once, calibrates within the time-out and only then reports ready.
The power-on flag is set by every reset and cleared only by a clear request seen while out of reset.
The detector events do not depend on the solver step or integration method beyond two solver steps.
